parts.name: EDUP 8-port unmanaged 2.5GbE switch
parts.vendor: Shenzhen Edup Electronics Technology Co., Ltd.
parts.plain_language: A cheap 2.5GbE switch is enough for routing independent inference jobs and moving models between nodes. It is not fast enough to make Ethernet behave like local RAM, so model sharding should remain a fallback rather than the default design.

parts.name: Optfocus 8-port fanless unmanaged 2.5GBASE-T switch
parts.plain_language: This costs a little more than the cheapest switch listing but comes from a long-established Alibaba supplier in the current results and is a reasonable reference option for a quiet eight-node cluster.

parts.name: 32GB DDR5-5600 SO-DIMM
parts.plain_language: Two 32GB sticks are the practical 64GB target for many nodes. Because memory is central to LLM capacity and stability, confirm JEDEC support, actual DRAM manufacturer, return policy and a memory-test result rather than buying purely on the headline price.

parts.name: M.2 PCIe NVMe SSD family, 1TB/2TB/4TB variants
parts.plain_language: Model storage does not need an exotic flagship SSD. Capacity, sustained reliability and honest NAND/firmware matter more. This listing is kept as a market-price lead only because the current result does not expose the exact per-capacity price.

parts.name: Intel N100 dual-LAN mini PC / control-plane node
parts.network: many current variants offer dual or multi 2.5GbE
parts.expandability: limited; best treated as router/control plane
parts.power_range_w: roughly 6-15W platform class; exact wall power varies
parts.plain_language: Do not buy an N100 because it looks good at LLM generation. Buy it because an always-on router, scheduler, monitoring node and model registry should consume very little energy and should not steal RAM or CPU time from inference workers. Keeping the control plane separate also makes the cluster more resilient.
parts.source_notes: Current Alibaba N100 listings span roughly US$75-133 for simple MOQ-1 systems, with many dual/multi-2.5GbE variants.
